title: The Rootbound Chapel of Greenhollow
theme: Enchanted forest ruin wrapped around an old stone chapel
hook: A hunter followed singing lights into Greenhollow and returned with leaves growing from their shadow. The village asks the party to enter the chapel ruin before the next moonrise claims more people.
background: The chapel marked a pact between villagers and forest spirits. A woodcutter lord broke the pact by stealing the chapel bell, and now roots, fey signs, beasts, and old stone wards are trying to decide whether the village still deserves mercy.

connections.note: Hidden root stair under the choir stones

playerSafe.description: A mossy ruined chapel swallowed by old trees, with visible stone chambers and forest paths but no marked secrets.

layout.notes: Open forest keyed-area map with clearings, landmarks, trails, and overgrown ruin fragments.

rooms.name: Briar-Latched Gate
rooms.readAloud: A leaning stone gate stands in a wall of thorn and ivy. Tiny lights blink between the leaves like watchful eyes.
rooms.gmNotes: The briars part for anyone who speaks respectfully to the chapel or offers water to the roots.

inhabitants.name: Thorn-Touched Pixies
inhabitants.tactics: Distract with lights, tangle packs, retreat into thorns
inhabitants.morale: Scatter if treated kindly or if iron is shown
inhabitants.wants: Proof the party is not here to cut or burn
inhabitants.leverage: They love songs, honey, and promises made aloud

rooms.treasure: A silver leaf token caught in the gate latch.
rooms.secrets: The lights repeat the route to the old choir in a three-note pattern.
rooms.exits: Root path to Room 2, mossy side path to Room 6.

rooms.name: Moon-Moss Narthex
rooms.readAloud: Broken flagstones glow under a carpet of blue-green moss. Root shadows move even when the wind is still.
rooms.gmNotes: Stepping only on glowing moss avoids a root snare. The hidden stair to Room 5 opens if the old pact verse is spoken.
rooms.treasure: A cracked pilgrim bowl that keeps water cool and clean.
rooms.secrets: A hidden root stair under the choir stones curls down to Room 5.
rooms.exits: Gate path to Room 1, chapel aisle to Room 3, hidden root stair to Room 5.

rooms.name: Fallen Saint Garden
rooms.readAloud: A toppled statue lies beneath flowering vines. Bees hum inside its hollow chest, and carved saints wear crowns of leaves.
rooms.gmNotes: The bees are calm unless the statue is struck. The statue remembers who stole the bell, but answers only in plant signs.

inhabitants.name: Honey-Drunk Forest Beasts
inhabitants.tactics: Warn first, charge intruders who harm the garden
inhabitants.morale: Calm if fed or if the statue is respected
inhabitants.wants: Quiet, flowers, and the bell returned
inhabitants.leverage: Fresh fruit or gentle repair earns safe passage

rooms.treasure: A saint medallion buried in a flower bed.
rooms.secrets: Pollen on the statue points toward the bell thief family crest.
rooms.exits: West to Room 2, root-wrapped arch to Room 4.

rooms.name: Bell-Oak Crossing
rooms.readAloud: A huge oak grows through a collapsed bell tower. Its branches hold a green-bronze bell that tolls without sound.
rooms.gmNotes: The silent bell reveals the final answer if rung with wood, not metal. A harsh strike calls angry roots.

inhabitants.name: Rootbound Chapel Guardian
inhabitants.tactics: Pin intruders with roots, shield the bell, shove foes from broken stairs
inhabitants.morale: Stops if the stolen bell story is acknowledged
inhabitants.wants: The pact restored and the bell left unharmed
inhabitants.leverage: The guardian obeys anyone carrying the silver leaf token

rooms.treasure: A green-bronze bell tongue wrapped in living bark.
rooms.secrets: The bell is a witness, not the source of the curse.
rooms.exits: Root-wrapped arch to Room 3, broken stair to Room 5.

rooms.name: Choir of Listening Roots
rooms.readAloud: Roots hang from the ceiling like organ pipes. Whispered memories pass through them in voices too old to place.
rooms.gmNotes: This room can reveal the twist: the village profited from the broken pact and hid the stolen bell in the manor.

inhabitants.name: Greenhollow Root Chorus
inhabitants.tactics: Ask binding questions, reveal shameful memories, block exits with roots
inhabitants.morale: Listen if the party admits uncertainty
inhabitants.wants: A true promise about the stolen bell
inhabitants.leverage: They cannot resist a sincerely spoken apology

rooms.treasure: A seed pearl grown around a chapel note.
rooms.secrets: The hidden root stair climbs back to Room 2; the roots know the bell was stolen by the woodcutter lord.
rooms.exits: Broken stair to Room 4, mossy aisle to Room 6, hidden root stair to Room 2.

rooms.name: Greenhollow Reliquary
rooms.readAloud: A roofless reliquary opens to the stars. Ferns grow around an empty bell cradle, and a circle of stones waits in silence.
rooms.gmNotes: The ending can be combat, bargaining, or oath repair. The forest wants a public promise and the bell returned, not blood.

inhabitants.name: The Chapel-Wood Spirit
inhabitants.tactics: Split the ground, dim lights, command beasts and roots
inhabitants.morale: Accepts a binding vow and proof the bell will be returned
inhabitants.wants: Restored pact, truthful memory, and protection for the old trees
inhabitants.leverage: It must honor promises made inside the reliquary circle

rooms.treasure: A blessing of safe passage through Greenhollow, the seed pearl reward, and village gratitude if the truth is carried home.
rooms.secrets: The reliquary stones show the woodcutter lord receiving the stolen bell from frightened priests.
rooms.exits: Mossy side path to Room 1, mossy aisle to Room 5, deer trail back to Greenhollow village.

wandering.result: Thorn-touched pixies test the party with a harmless but annoying trick
Forest beasts follow at the edge of torchlight
A root snare tightens across the next doorway
A lost villager whispers from behind a tree that was not there before
Fey lights mark a safe path, then split into two trails
The silent bell tolls and every plant leans toward Room 4

environmental.result: Falling leaves briefly spell a warning
A stone shifts underfoot and exposes old roots
Birdsong repeats something the party just said
The forest grows quiet before a guardian arrives

complications.result: A promise spoken casually begins to bind
Roots separate the rear of the group for a scene
A helpful fey asks for a memory as payment
The guardian mistakes the party for bell thieves
A clue grows over with moss unless copied quickly
The village bell rings far away at the wrong time

treasureTable.result: Silver leaf token that opens thorn gates
Pilgrim bowl that keeps water cool and clean
Saint medallion wrapped in flowering vine
Green-bronze bell tongue wrapped in living bark
Seed pearl grown around a confession note
Forest blessing and proof of the broken pact

gmNotes: Make the ruin feel watchful rather than hostile at first.
Most encounters can be softened through respect, gifts, or truthful promises.
The twist is that the village benefited from the stolen bell and forgot on purpose.
A strong ending asks the party what promise they are willing to carry back into public.
